## Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Industrial and Electronics have wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%; negative lower-tail margins motivate improving difficult predictions. These training diagnostics do not establish validation performance. (2) Users report stale-interest recommendations and broadly relevant items they would defer. Immediate-next-choice supervision plausibly addresses both, but cannot establish compatibility, ownership, quantity needs, or current mood. (3) Embedding scores near 0.5 imply approximately zero mean cosine similarity, providing no evidence for collapse regularization. Unidentified-item skips must remain separate from explicit preference rejections.

**Literature insights.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already mixes terminal and random masking. Its reference generator produces ten random-mask copies plus one terminal copy; record proportions differ from supervised-token loss weights. (2) The [replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483) identifies training duration as a substantial confound. (3) [RSS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates examining endpoint recency, but uses a different objective. (4) [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) and [AHNS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05191) motivate negative coverage and controlled hardness without establishing transfer to this benchmark.

## Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Atomic experiment | Intended failure addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Prediction alignment | Increase terminal supervision on existing training windows | Historical relevance outweighs present choice |
| Historical coverage | Sample historical prefixes; vary endpoint recency separately | Recent specific interests receive insufficient emphasis |
| Candidate discrimination | Gradually introduce moderate hard negatives | Confusing candidates outrank positives |
| Item specificity | Jointly learn gated title/description embeddings | Broad resemblance obscures specific connections |

Scores are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / difficulty; difficulty 10 means hardest. Alignment scores describe hypotheses.

- **Terminal-supervision weighting: 2/6/7/7/3.** Originality + targeted weighting experiment; − established masking strategy. Potential + cheap foundation; − baseline may already suffice. User + addresses stale interests and deferred broad matches; − no compatibility guarantee. Model + targets next-choice separation; − gains uncertain. Difficulty + small sampler change; − requires exposure accounting.
- **Prefix-endpoint sampling: 3/6/7/6/4.** Originality + historical coverage within BERT4Rec; − related sampling precedents. Potential + tests recency; − dataset dependent. User + emphasizes recent specific interests; − recency can amplify noise. Model + adds prediction contexts; − changes context lengths. Difficulty + simple sampling; − several confounds.
- **Moderate-negative curriculum: 4/7/6/9/5.** Originality + controlled-hardness transfer; − established principle. Potential + targets lower-tail errors; − false negatives persist. User + distinguishes alternatives; − hardness does not encode usefulness. Model + targets wrong ranks; − sampled-candidate overfitting. Difficulty + unchanged architecture; − mining cost.
- **Gated text embeddings: 4/6/8/6/6.** Originality + compliant joint text learning; − established pattern. Potential + represents specific attributes; − sparse supervision. User + captures identifiers/artists; − ownership remains unknown. Model + may distinguish similar IDs; − unverified. Difficulty + single network; − tokenization and predictor changes.

## Selected experiment

At 0% progress, select **increased terminal-supervision weighting**, narrowing the original prefix-terminal proposal to avoid changing endpoint sampling simultaneously. It targets stale interests and broadly plausible but deferrable recommendations, plus weak positive–negative separation. Preserve baseline window/user sampling; alternate terminal-only and baseline random-mask batches 1:1, averaging supervised-token losses within each batch. Terminal examples replace the existing window’s final item with MASK. Historical-prefix sampling remains a separate follow-up: choose a training target, discard its suffix, and mask it; uniform endpoints change both historical coverage and context lengths.

Compare against the corrected baseline with architecture, loss, optimizer, negatives and checkpoint rule fixed. Report updates, supervised targets, visible-context lengths and GPU seconds: equal updates do not ensure equal supervision or compute. Equal-target and equal-time comparisons are secondary controls only if the shared budget permits; they must retain the epoch/update caps.

Keep one checkpoint/category, routing, seeds 0/42, maximum 200 epochs × 200 batches, left padding and appended-mask inference. Use final-nonpadding readout. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, seed 42. Report category results and all selection attempts. [Sampled HR](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) does not establish full-catalog quality. If paired hit vectors are available, report a stratified paired percentile bootstrap interval, 10,000 replicates, seed 42; it excludes training variability and adaptive-selection bias. Treat gains as exploratory, freeze configuration before held-out evaluation, and preserve separate qualitative checks for immediate choice and explicit incompatibility. No gains are claimed.

"""Per-dataset BERT4Rec baseline for Amazon Reviews.

Trains one independent BERT4Rec checkpoint per dataset while sharing one default
hyper-parameter profile across datasets. The generated predict.py routes by the
optional dataset_name keyword used by the RecHarness Amazon Reviews harness.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import math
import os
import pickle
import random
from collections import defaultdict

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

DEFAULT_DATASETS = [
    "Movies_and_TV",
    "Industrial_and_Scientific",
    "Electronics",
    "CDs_and_Vinyl",
]
DATASETS = [
    part.strip()
    for part in os.environ.get("GAGC_DATASETS", ",".join(DEFAULT_DATASETS)).split(",")
    if part.strip()
]

DATA_DIR = os.environ["GAGC_DATA_DIR"]

SEED = 42
### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END
random.seed(SEED)
np.random.seed(SEED)
torch.manual_seed(SEED)
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(SEED)


def _read_split(path: str) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
    data: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.strip().split()
            if len(parts) == 2:
                data[int(parts[0])].append(int(parts[1]))
    return dict(data)


def _load_itemnum(data_dir: str, dataset_name: str) -> int:
    stats_path = os.path.join(data_dir, "dataset_stats.json")
    if os.path.isfile(stats_path):
        with open(stats_path) as f:
            stats = json.load(f)
        if dataset_name in stats:
            return int(stats[dataset_name]["itemnum"])
    itemnum = 0
    for split in ("train", "valid"):
        path = os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_{split}.txt")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                parts = line.strip().split()
                if len(parts) == 2:
                    itemnum = max(itemnum, int(parts[1]))
    return itemnum


def load_dataset(dataset_name: str, data_dir: str):
    user_train = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_train.txt"))
    user_valid = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_valid.txt"))
    itemnum = _load_itemnum(data_dir, dataset_name)
    return user_train, user_valid, itemnum

def sample_batch(
    user_train: dict[int, list[int]],
    itemnum: int,
    batch_size: int,
    maxlen: int,
    terminal_only: bool = False,
):
    # Keep uniform eligible-user sampling and the existing final-window endpoints.
    if maxlen < 2:
        raise ValueError("BERT4Rec training requires maxlen >= 2")
    users = [u for u, items in user_train.items() if len(items) >= 2]
    if not users:
        raise RuntimeError("no users with at least two training interactions")
    batch_seq, batch_pos, batch_neg = [], [], []
    for _ in range(batch_size):
        history = user_train[random.choice(users)]
        items = history[-maxlen:]
        seq = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        pos = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        neg = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
        seq[-len(items) :] = items
        if terminal_only:
            # Replace the existing endpoint; never expose a shifted target.
            selected = [maxlen - 1]
        else:
            eligible = list(range(maxlen - len(items), maxlen))
            selected = [i for i in eligible if random.random() < 0.2]
            if not selected:
                selected = [random.choice(eligible)]
            if random.random() < 0.5 and maxlen - 1 not in selected:
                selected.append(maxlen - 1)
        interacted = set(history)
        if len(interacted) >= itemnum:
            raise RuntimeError("no unobserved negative item available")
        for i in selected:
            pos[i] = seq[i]
            seq[i] = itemnum + 1
            item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
            while item in interacted:
                item = random.randint(1, itemnum)
            neg[i] = item
        batch_seq.append(seq)
        batch_pos.append(pos)
        batch_neg.append(neg)
    return np.asarray(batch_seq), np.asarray(batch_pos), np.asarray(batch_neg)

        dropout_rate: float = 0.2,
        maxlen: int = 128,
    ):

        self.pos_emb = nn.Embedding(maxlen + 1, hidden_units, padding_idx=0)

            d_model=hidden_units,
            nhead=num_heads,
            dim_feedforward=hidden_units * 4,
            dropout=dropout_rate,
            activation="gelu",
            batch_first=True,
            norm_first=True,
        )
        self.encoder = nn.TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_layers=num_blocks)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        with torch.no_grad():
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.item_emb.weight)
            self.item_emb.weight[0].zero_()
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(self.pos_emb.weight)
            self.pos_emb.weight[0].zero_()

    def encode_sequence(self, seq: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        batch, length = seq.shape

        pos = pos * (seq != 0).long()
        x = self.item_emb(seq) * (self.hidden_units**0.5) + self.pos_emb(pos)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        padding = seq == 0
        safe_padding = padding.clone()
        safe_padding[padding.all(dim=1), -1] = False
        x = self.encoder(x, src_key_padding_mask=safe_padding)
        return self.norm(x)

    def forward(self, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor):
        out = self.encode_sequence(seq)
        pos_scores = (out * self.item_emb(pos)).sum(dim=-1)
        neg_scores = (out * self.item_emb(neg)).sum(dim=-1)
        return pos_scores, neg_scores

    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Preserve diagnostic interfaces and appended-mask readout
    def log2feats(self, sequence: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Diagnostic batches already contain masked targets; do not append here.
        return self.encode_sequence(sequence)

    def predict_score(
        self, features: torch.Tensor, items: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Supports aligned B x L targets and shared candidate lists.
        return (features * self.item_emb(items)).sum(dim=-1)

    def score_candidates(
        self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Left-padded histories: retain the final MAXLEN-1 items and append MASK.
        prediction_seq = torch.zeros_like(seq)
        prediction_seq[:, :-1] = seq[:, 1:]
        prediction_seq[:, -1] = self.mask_token

        positions = torch.arange(seq.shape[1], device=seq.device).expand_as(seq)
        last = positions.masked_fill(prediction_seq == 0, -1).amax(dim=1)
        features = out[torch.arange(seq.shape[0], device=seq.device), last]
        if candidates.ndim == 1:
            scores = self.predict_score(features[:, None, :], candidates)
        else:
            scores = self.predict_score(features[:, None, :], candidates)
        return scores[0] if seq.shape[0] == 1 else scores

    def _encode_events(self, events, length):
        mask = int(self.network.mask_token)
        if len(events) > length - 1:
            raise ValueError("freeze and truncate the prefix before intervention")
        sequence = np.zeros(length, dtype=np.int64)
        if events:
            sequence[length - len(events) - 1 : length - 1] = [
                item for _, item in events
            ]
        sequence[-1] = mask
        assert np.count_nonzero(sequence == mask) == 1
        assert np.count_nonzero(sequence) == len(events) + 1
        return sequence

    @staticmethod
    def _score_summary(scores, candidates):
        target = scores[0]
        # One-based average rank; deterministic item-ID tie breaking only for top10 sets.
        rank = 1.0 + float(np.sum(scores[1:] > target))
        rank += 0.5 * float(np.sum(scores[1:] == target))
        order = np.lexsort((candidates, -scores))
        boundary = float(np.sort(scores[1:])[-10])
        margin = float(target - boundary)
        scale = float(np.std(scores))
        return {
            "rank": rank,
            "hr10": float(rank <= 10.0),
            "raw_margin": margin,
            "standardized_margin": margin / scale if scale > 1e-12 else None,
            "zero_variance": scale <= 1e-12,
            "top10": set(int(i) for i in candidates[order[:10]]),
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _time_values(values):
        if values is None:
            return None
        try:
            result = np.asarray([float(v) for v in values], dtype=np.float64)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            try:
                dates = np.asarray(values, dtype="datetime64[ms]")
                if np.isnat(dates).any():
                    return None
                result = dates.astype(np.int64).astype(np.float64)
            except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
                return None
        return result if np.isfinite(result).all() else None

    def _prefix_interventions(self):
        histories = self.user_train.get("History", {})
        timestamps = self.user_train.get("Time", {})
        if not isinstance(histories, dict):
            raise ValueError("ModelView.user_train must contain a History mapping")
        if not isinstance(timestamps, dict):
            timestamps = {}
        itemnum = int(self.network.itemnum)
        length = int(self.network.maxlen)
        if length < 3:
            return {
                "available": False,
                "reason": "requires at least two visible events and MASK",
            }
        category = getattr(self.model, "dataset_name", None)
        if category is None:
            category = getattr(self.network, "dataset_name", None)
        category = (
            str(category) if category is not None else "current_category_unlabeled"
        )
        selection_rng = random.Random(42)
        candidate_rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
        edit_rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
        bootstrap_rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
        users = sorted(histories, key=lambda u: (str(type(u)), str(u)))
        sampled_users = selection_rng.sample(users, min(200, len(users)))
        counts = {
            "training_users": len(users),
            "sampled_users": len(sampled_users),
            "short_history": 0,
            "invalid_item_ids": 0,
            "insufficient_negatives": 0,
            "evaluated_users": 0,
            "identity_checks": 0,
            "identity_failures": 0,
        }
        records = []
        baseline_records = []
        catalog = np.arange(1, itemnum + 1, dtype=np.int64)
        for user in sampled_users:
            try:
                history = [int(item) for item in histories[user]]
            except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError):
                counts["invalid_item_ids"] += 1
                continue
            if len(history) < 3:
                counts["short_history"] += 1
                continue
            if any(item < 1 or item > itemnum for item in history):
                counts["invalid_item_ids"] += 1
                continue
            # Last training event is the target EVENT; matching earlier item IDs are valid.
            target_index = len(history) - 1
            start = max(0, target_index - (length - 1))
            visible = list(enumerate(history[start:target_index], start=start))
            if len(visible) < 2:
                counts["short_history"] += 1
                continue
            assert all(index < target_index for index, _ in visible)
            target = history[target_index]
            excluded = np.asarray(
                sorted({target} | {item for _, item in visible}), dtype=np.int64
            )
            # Catalog is already ordered and unique; avoid repeated sorting.
            eligible_mask = np.ones(itemnum, dtype=bool)
            eligible_mask[excluded - 1] = False
            eligible = catalog[eligible_mask]
            if len(eligible) < 99:
                counts["insufficient_negatives"] += 1
                continue
            candidates = np.concatenate(
                (
                    np.asarray([target]),
                    candidate_rng.choice(eligible, 99, replace=False),
                )
            )
            assert len(np.unique(candidates)) == 100
            assert not (set(candidates[1:]) & {item for _, item in visible})
            baseline_tensor = self._encode_events(visible, length)
            n = len(visible)
            k = min(3, n // 2)
            recent_indices = set(range(n - k, n))
            oldest_indices = set(range(k))
            branches = [("baseline", visible), ("identity", list(visible))]
            branches.append(
                (
                    "delete_recent_compact",
                    [e for i, e in enumerate(visible) if i not in recent_indices],
                )
            )
            branches.append(
                (
                    "delete_oldest_compact",
                    [e for i, e in enumerate(visible) if i not in oldest_indices],
                )
            )
            for _ in range(10):
                removed = set(int(i) for i in edit_rng.choice(n, k, replace=False))
                branches.append(
                    (
                        "delete_random_compact",
                        [e for i, e in enumerate(visible) if i not in removed],
                    )
                )
            window = min(5, n)
            for _ in range(10):
                order = edit_rng.permutation(window)
                edited = visible[:-window] + [
                    visible[n - window + int(i)] for i in order
                ]
                branches.append(("permute_recent_order_stress", edited))
            arrays = np.stack(
                [self._encode_events(events, length) for _, events in branches]
            )
            for _, events in branches:
                assert all(
                    index < target_index and history[index] == item
                    for index, item in events
                )
            sequence = torch.as_tensor(arrays, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
            features = self._features(sequence)
            positions = torch.arange(length, device=self.device).expand_as(sequence)
            last = positions.masked_fill(sequence == 0, -1).amax(dim=1)
            assert bool(
                torch.all(sequence.gather(1, last[:, None]) == self.network.mask_token)
            )
            if features.ndim != 3 or tuple(features.shape[:2]) != tuple(sequence.shape):
                raise RuntimeError("log2feats must return aligned B x L x H features")
            readout = features[torch.arange(len(branches), device=self.device), last]
            items = torch.as_tensor(candidates, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
            logits = (
                self._scores(readout[:, None, :], items).detach().float().cpu().numpy()
            )
            if logits.shape != (len(branches), 100) or not np.isfinite(logits).all():
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "incompatible or nonfinite BERT4Rec intervention scores"
                )
            counts["identity_checks"] += 1
            if not np.allclose(logits[0], logits[1], rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6):
                counts["identity_failures"] += 1
                raise RuntimeError("identity intervention failed score reproducibility")
            base = self._score_summary(logits[0], candidates)
            baseline_records.append(base)
            raw_times = timestamps.get(user, timestamps.get(str(user)))
            if raw_times is not None and len(raw_times) == len(history):
                times = self._time_values(raw_times)
            else:
                times = None
            user_record = {}
            for branch_index, (name, events) in enumerate(branches[1:], start=1):
                summary = self._score_summary(logits[branch_index], candidates)
                effective = not np.array_equal(arrays[branch_index], baseline_tensor)
                if name.startswith("delete_"):
                    edit_distance = n - len(events)
                else:
                    edit_distance = sum(a[0] != b[0] for a, b in zip(visible, events))
                inversion_count = None
                if name == "permute_recent_order_stress" and times is not None:
                    # Measured chronological availability violations among surviving events.
                    ordered_times = [times[index] for index, _ in events]
                    inversion_count = sum(
                        int(ordered_times[i] > ordered_times[j])
                        for i in range(len(events))
                        for j in range(i + 1, len(events))
                    )
                delta = {
                    "hr10": summary["hr10"] - base["hr10"],
                    "rank": summary["rank"] - base["rank"],
                    "raw_margin": summary["raw_margin"] - base["raw_margin"],
                    "standardized_margin": (
                        summary["standardized_margin"] - base["standardized_margin"]
                        if summary["standardized_margin"] is not None
                        and base["standardized_margin"] is not None
                        else None
                    ),
                }
                user_record.setdefault(name, []).append(
                    {
                        "delta": delta,
                        "effective": effective,
                        "zero_variance": summary["zero_variance"],
                        "overlap": len(base["top10"] & summary["top10"]) / 10.0,
                        "edit_distance": edit_distance,
                        "timestamp_inversions": inversion_count,
                        "baseline_correct": bool(base["hr10"]),
                        "history_length": n,
                    }
                )
            records.append(user_record)
        counts["evaluated_users"] = len(records)
        result = {
            "available": bool(records),
            "source": "training_prefix_in_sample_dependence",
            "category": category,
            "checkpoint_count": 1,
            "seed": 42,
            "counts": counts,
            "branches": {},
            "validation_usefulness": {
                "available": False,
                "reason": "No explicitly authorized pinned validation diagnostic protocol is supplied by ModelView/train_loader.",
            },
            "position_preserving_deletion": {
                "available": False,
                "reason": "Supplied BERT4Rec/ModelView has no explicit position_ids-capable diagnostic path; compact deletion only.",
            },
            "cross_category_macro": {
                "available": False,
                "reason": "This probe observes one category; four-category macro effects require all four category records.",
            },
            "bootstrap_replicates": 1000,
        }
        if not records:
            result["baseline"] = None
            return result
        result["baseline"] = {}
        for key in ("rank", "hr10", "raw_margin", "standardized_margin"):
            values = [row[key] for row in baseline_records if row[key] is not None]
            result["baseline"][key] = {
                "mean": float(np.mean(values)) if values else None,
                "users": len(values),
            }
        result["baseline"]["zero_variance_users"] = sum(
            int(row["zero_variance"]) for row in baseline_records
        )
        # One shared set of complete-user resamples preserves dependence across all draws/branches.
        resamples = bootstrap_rng.integers(0, len(records), size=(1000, len(records)))
        for name in records[0]:
            user_draws = [record[name] for record in records]
            draws = [draw for rows in user_draws for draw in rows]
            report = {
                "users": len(user_draws),
                "draws": len(draws),
                "no_op_draws": sum(int(not row["effective"]) for row in draws),
                "zero_variance_draws": sum(int(row["zero_variance"]) for row in draws),
                "top10_overlap": float(np.mean([row["overlap"] for row in draws])),
                "mean_event_edit_distance": float(
                    np.mean([row["edit_distance"] for row in draws])
                ),
                "paired_effects": {},
                "strata": {},
            }
            measured_times = [
                row["timestamp_inversions"]
                for row in draws
                if row["timestamp_inversions"] is not None
            ]
            report["temporal_availability"] = {
                "available": bool(measured_times),
                "draws": len(measured_times),
                "draws_with_inversions": sum(int(v > 0) for v in measured_times),
                "mean_inversions": (
                    float(np.mean(measured_times)) if measured_times else None
                ),
            }
            for key in ("hr10", "rank", "raw_margin", "standardized_margin"):
                means, effective_means = [], []
                for rows in user_draws:
                    valid = [
                        row["delta"][key]
                        for row in rows
                        if row["delta"][key] is not None
                    ]
                    effective = [
                        row["delta"][key]
                        for row in rows
                        if row["effective"] and row["delta"][key] is not None
                    ]
                    means.append(float(np.mean(valid)) if valid else np.nan)
                    if effective:
                        effective_means.append(float(np.mean(effective)))
                values = np.asarray(means, dtype=np.float64)
                sampled = values[resamples]
                finite_counts = np.isfinite(sampled).sum(axis=1)
                boot = np.divide(
                    np.nansum(sampled, axis=1),
                    finite_counts,
                    out=np.full(1000, np.nan),
                    where=finite_counts > 0,
                )
                boot = boot[np.isfinite(boot)]
                finite = values[np.isfinite(values)]
                report["paired_effects"][key] = {
                    "mean_delta": float(finite.mean()) if len(finite) else None,
                    "users": len(finite),
                    "exploratory_paired_user_95pct_interval": (
                        np.percentile(boot, [2.5, 97.5]).tolist() if len(boot) else None
                    ),
                    "valid_bootstrap_replicates": len(boot),
                    "effective_edit_mean_delta": (
                        float(np.mean(effective_means)) if effective_means else None
                    ),
                    "effective_edit_users": len(effective_means),
                }
            selectors = {
                "baseline_correct": lambda row: (
                    "correct" if row["baseline_correct"] else "incorrect"
                ),
                "history_length": lambda row: (
                    "2-5"
                    if row["history_length"] <= 5
                    else ("6-20" if row["history_length"] <= 20 else "21+")
                ),
                "event_edit_distance": lambda row: str(row["edit_distance"]),

                        np.mean(group.pop("user_mean_deltas"))
                    )
                report["strata"][stratum] = groups
            result["branches"][name] = report
        return result
